sanity_expectations: Exact symmetry check: when u1 = u2, the correction term is zero and v_post should equal that common input velocity for any positive m1,m2.
Momentum-average baseline should be recovered approximately when |u1-u2| is small compared with |(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2)|.
At fixed m1,m2 and similar nonzero v_cm, increasing |u1-u2| should generally increase the magnitude of the dissipative correction away from the momentum-average value.
At similar normalized slip and v_cm, near-equal masses (m1≈m2, symmetry factor near 1) should show a stronger mid-range deviation from the momentum-average baseline than strongly unequal masses.
Sampling must avoid or resample cases with m1*u1 + m2*u2 too close to 0, because the expression contains division by the center-of-mass velocity and becomes ill-conditioned there.
role_corrections: v_post: claimed-output/target derivative -> dependent variable (confirmed; algebraic target, no derivatives present)
m1: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (overridden: static sampled input axis, not a time axis)
m2: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (overridden: static sampled input axis, not a time axis)
u1: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (overridden: static sampled input axis, not a time axis)
u2: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable (overridden: static sampled input axis, not a time axis)
rationale: Structure check shows a static algebraic relation with free symbols {m1,m2,u1,u2,v_post}, no derivatives, no integrals, and no extra latent functions, so this is an explicit mapping from four sampled inputs to one output. Because freedom_change is none and the labels already treat m1,m2,u1,u2 as inputs, preserve them as sampled axes rather than fixed parameters. The expression contains the normalized slip ratio (u1-u2)/v_cm with v_cm=(m1*u1+m2*u2)/(m1+m2), so the main numerical hazard is v_cm≈0, not large magnitudes. Chosen mass ranges 0.5–3 kg span near-equal and unequal mass ratios, making the symmetry factor 4*m1*m2/(m1+m2)^2 vary substantially without extreme conditioning. Chosen velocity ranges -2.5 to 2.5 m/s include same-direction and opposing approaches, producing small to moderate and larger relative-speed contrasts. To expose the intended curvature changes rather than mostly singular or recovery cases, sampling should reject or resample points with |v_cm|<0.2 m/s; this keeps the normalized ratio finite while still allowing low-to-moderate |v_cm| where the added higher-order loss is visible. Within the accepted set, the dataset will contain comparisons at similar v_cm but different u1-u2, and comparisons at similar normalized slip across different mass-symmetry classes, directly matching the recorded distinguishing conditions. No observation noise should be added.
